acceptance: Each maintenance operation issues a bounded number of statements independent of row count: a test with a statement-counting connection shows the count is the same at 10 and 10,000 rows.

With the same configured seed (deterministic after tpcds-maintenance-timer-hygiene-20261103), post-maintenance table row counts and per-column checksums equal those produced by the per-row implementation on the base commit, on DuckDB at SF0.01.
Maintenance time at SF1 on DuckDB drops measurably; before and after durations on the same host are pasted in the PR.
No set-based work is moved outside the timed interval; a boundary test shows the statements run between the interval's start and stop.

If docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md exists on the base branch, update the rows this change affects; otherwise append the row text to the context of tpc-measured-intervals-reference-20261103. Changelog fragment notes the performance change.

description:
Replace per-row maintenance statements with set-based SQL for the synthetic maintenance path. This item survives only if the owner keeps that path (option B or C in tpcds-maintenance-data-source-decision-20261103). Under option A the per-row UPDATE handlers are deleted and tpcds-maintenance-dsdgen-refresh-data-20261103 implements the spec functions as set-based SQL, so this item is closed as superseded when the decision is recorded. Do not start before the decision is recorded; the hygiene item makes the generator deterministic so before/after checksums are comparable.

Facts (benchbox/core/tpcds/maintenance_operations.py; re-read before editing): _update_customer, _update_item, _update_inventory and _bulk_update_inventory send one parameterized UPDATE per row (one round trip per row on cloud warehouses); sales inserts build rows with Python random and send 100-row VALUES batches; _insert_returns_generic fetchall()s sales rows into Python and rebuilds them. TPC-DS 4.0.0 clauses 5.2.5 and 5.2.7 keep loading and staging inside the timed maintenance interval, so set-based SQL and staged loads both stay inside the timer.

Change: use set-based SQL (UPDATE ... FROM (SELECT ...), INSERT ... SELECT) or the staged load from the dsdgen item, keeping results deterministic for a fixed refresh data set.

Guardrails for all code work: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone. No explanatory comments or docstrings in source (make comment-policy-check). Durations use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()/elapsed_seconds(). Add a changelog.d/ fragment. Cited line numbers are orientation only: re-read the named symbols, docs and spec clauses before editing and treat a mismatch as a reason to stop and update this item. No live-cloud runs without owner approval; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point. Green focused tests are not release certification.
